  "concordance_definition": "The paper states that \"zebrafish can be used to eliminate potentially unsafe compounds rapidly in the early stages of drug development and to prioritize compounds for further preclinical and clinical studies.\" and \"zebrafish pharmacologic responses to well-characterized cardiotoxins are strikingly similar to responses in humans\". For developmental toxicity, it states \"assay predictivity and accuracy were assessed\" and \"this assay format presented a 75% success rate in identifying nonteratogenic compounds and a 100% success rate in identifying teratogens\".",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Full validation will require assessment of a large number of compounds from diverse classes.",
    "Although zebrafish and mammalian hearts differ in structure and zebrafish lack a pulmonary system, they exhibit similar functional characteristics.",
    "It is unclear how ADME after drug delivery in fish water compares to ADME after delivery by other routes of administration.",
    "Reported results show that inter- and intra-laboratory standards vary widely, confounding interpretation of drug-induced toxicity and limiting wider acceptance of this model organism."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "Both authors are employees of Phylonix. Ms McGrath is also an inventor of patents assigned to Phylonix.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "A single zebrafish spawning produces 100-200 eggs.",
    "Adult zebrafish are 3-cm long.",
    "Larvae are 1-4-mm long.",
    "Zebrafish ERG and human ERG are 99% conserved.",
    "One hundred small molecules were tested for QT prolongation; 22 of 23 drugs that cause QT prolongation in humans consistently caused bradycardia and blocked AV conduction in zebrafish.",
    "Cost of ECG testing: $1.00 per zebrafish versus $100 per rodent, and >$1000 per dog.",
    "CYP3A4 was upregulated in zebrafish treated with dexamethasone, similar to the CYP3A4 response in humans.",
    "GFAP level increased more than twofold in zebrafish treated with TCDD.",
    "The assay for developmental toxicity presented a 75% success rate in identifying nonteratogenic compounds and a 100% success rate in identifying teratogens.",
    "The assay was ranked good (>70% <80%) for specificity and excellent (>80%) for sensitivity for developmental toxicity."
  ]
